prompt:
A sealed container holds a mixture of helium-4 gas (mass of atom m_He = 6.64 x 10^-27 kg) and argon-40 gas (mass of atom m_Ar = 6.64 x 10^-26 kg) in thermal equilibrium at a temperature of 127 degrees Celsius. Take the Boltzmann constant k = 1.38 x 10^-23 J K^-1.
(a) Calculate the thermodynamic temperature of the gas mixture. [1]
(b) Calculate the average translational kinetic energy of:
(i) a helium-4 atom; [1]
(ii) an argon-40 atom. [1]
(c) Calculate the root-mean-square speed c_rms of:
(i) a helium-4 atom; [2]
(ii) an argon-40 atom. [1]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the thermodynamic temperature of the gas mixture.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.prompt: Calculate the average translational kinetic energy of a helium-4 atom.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the average translational kinetic energy of an argon-40 atom.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.prompt: Calculate the root-mean-square speed c_rms of a helium-4 atom.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the root-mean-square speed c_rms of an argon-40 atom.

mark_scheme.criterion: (b)(ii) States 8.28 x 10^-21 J (identical to helium because temperature is identical).
(c)(i) Uses (1/2) m c_rms^2 = E_K to give c_rms = sqrt(2 E_K / m) and substitutes values.
(c)(ii) Calculates c_rms,Ar = c_rms,He / sqrt(10) = 1579 / 3.162 = 499 m s^-1 (accept 500 m s^-1).

part_enrichment.guidance: Convert Celsius to kelvin: T = 127 + 273.15 = 400.15 K (rounds to 400 K).
Substitute T = 400 K into E_K = (3/2) kT.
Because the mixture is in thermal equilibrium, both gases are at the exact same temperature, and E_K depends only on temperature.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Attempting to recalculate with a different mass and getting a different kinetic energy.

marking_points.criterion: Rearranges (1/2) m c_rms^2 = E_K to c_rms = sqrt(2 E_K / m).

part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Forgetting to take the square root of the mean-square speed.

marking_points.criterion: Calculates c_rms,Ar = 499 m s^-1 (or 500 m s^-1).

part_enrichment.guidance: Mass of argon is 10 times that of helium, so speed is smaller by factor sqrt(10): 1579 / 3.162 = 499 m s^-1.

hints: In (a), convert Celsius to kelvin by adding 273.
In (b), apply E_K = (3/2) kT and remember that both gases share the same temperature.
In (c), use c_rms = sqrt(2 E_K / m) for each gas.
solution:
(a) Thermodynamic temperature:
T = 127 + 273.15 = 400.15 K = 400 K.
(b)(i) For helium-4:
E_K = (3/2) kT = 1.5 * (1.38 x 10^-23 J K^-1) * (400 K) = 8.28 x 10^-21 J.
(ii) For argon-40:
Since the gases are in thermal equilibrium at the same temperature, argon atoms have the identical average translational kinetic energy:
E_K = 8.28 x 10^-21 J.
(c)(i) Root-mean-square speed of helium-4:
(1/2) m c_rms^2 = E_K => c_rms = sqrt(2 E_K / m)
c_rms,He = sqrt(2 * 8.28 x 10^-21 J / 6.64 x 10^-27 kg) = sqrt(2.494 x 10^6) = 1579 m s^-1 = 1.58 x 10^3 m s^-1.
(ii) Root-mean-square speed of argon-40:
c_rms,Ar = sqrt(2 * 8.28 x 10^-21 J / 6.64 x 10^-26 kg) = sqrt(2.494 x 10^5) = 499 m s^-1 (or 5.0 x 10^2 m s^-1).
teacher_walkthrough: Part (b): Emphasize that in thermal equilibrium, E_K is identical for all gases regardless of atomic mass: E_K = (3/2) kT = 8.28 x 10^-21 J.
Part (c): Lighter helium moves at 1580 m s^-1, while heavier argon moves at 499 m s^-1 (factor of sqrt(10) slower).
